intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the aurora borealis dancing across the sky. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind this natural phenomenon while capturing stunning photographs.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and swim-up bars while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the main lagoon, towel rental, and one silica mud mask.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. The surreal blue and green hues of the water make this one of the most unique natural experiences on Earth, guided by certified instructors.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a peaceful soak amid stunning Icelandic countryside.

experiences.name: Skaftafell Glacier Hike on Vatnajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier with an expert guide. Explore stunning ice formations, deep blue crevasses, and ash layers from ancient volcanic eruptions. The hike offers breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding black sand plains and mountain peaks.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the Flybus or a budget shuttle to Reykjavik BSI terminal, then arrange onward travel north toward Siglufjörður. The drive is approximately 4-5 hours via Route 1 and the Héðinsfjörður tunnel. Rest and recover from the flight during the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Siglufjörður in the early afternoon. Check in early if possible at Hotel Siglunes on Lækjargata 10, or store luggage and take a gentle walk along the harbour front to get oriented. Siglufjörður is a charming small fishing town nestled in a dramatic fjord — explore the colourful wooden houses and the quiet harbour area.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the hotel and rest after the long travel day. As darkness falls (which comes early in January), step outside or find a dark spot near the harbour to watch for the Northern Lights — January is prime aurora season in Iceland. Dress in all your warmest layers.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at Keflavik Airport before departure — budget around 1,500-2,000 ISK for a pastry and coffee.
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches or snacks from a Reykjavik Bonus or Krónan supermarket during your transit stop to save money on the road.
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — a cosy local café offering hearty Icelandic soups and simple meals. Budget around 2,500-3,500 ISK for a bowl of lamb soup and bread.

day_by_day.notes: January days in Siglufjörður are very short — expect only about 4-5 hours of daylight. The Héðinsfjörður tunnel (opened 2010) makes access much easier. Check road conditions at road.is before driving. Stock up on groceries in Akureyri or Reykjavik if passing through, as Siglufjörður has limited shopping options.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's most acclaimed regional museums, telling the story of the herring fishing boom that made Siglufjörður prosperous. It is spread across several restored buildings on the harbour. Entry is around 2,200 ISK for adults.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Siglufjörður town trail — a self-guided loop around the town taking in the old fish factories, the church, and viewpoints over the fjord. The surrounding mountains draped in snow create a stunning winter backdrop. Dress warmly and wear ice-grip footwear as paths can be icy.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights watch from the hillside above town or the harbour pier. Siglufjörður has very little light pollution and the surrounding mountains frame the sky beautifully. Check aurora forecasts at en.vedur.is and head out when the KP index is 2 or above.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel — pick up oats, yoghurt, and fruit from the local Samkaup store on Gránugata. Budget around 800 ISK.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket supplies — rye bread (rúgbrauð), skyr, and Icelandic cheese. Eaten at the museum café or a harbour bench.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple pasta or rice dish in the hotel kitchen if available, or visit Kaffi Rauðka again for their daily soup special. Budget 2,000-3,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: The Herring Era Museum may have reduced winter hours — confirm opening times by calling ahead or checking their website. Wear microspike crampons for icy walking paths, available cheaply at Icelandic hardware stores.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hofsós, approximately 45 minutes south along the Skagafjörður coast. Visit the Icelandic Emigration Centre (Vesturfarasetrið), which documents the mass emigration of Icelanders to North America in the 19th century. Entry is modest at around 1,500 ISK.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the tiny village of Hofsós and its dramatic coastal setting. The famous Hofsós infinity swimming pool (Sundlaug Hofsóss) overlooks the fjord — one of Iceland's most scenic public pools. Entry is around 1,000 ISK. Soak in the geothermally heated outdoor pool while gazing across Skagafjörður — a true budget hot spring experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður before dark. Spend the evening aurora hunting from the hotel or the quiet roads just outside town. The clear mountain air and low humidity in January make for excellent aurora viewing conditions.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — skyr with granola and coffee. Budget 600-800 ISK.
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of soup and sandwiches for the road trip — eat with a view of Skagafjörður.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at the hotel — buy a simple ready meal or ingredients from Samkaup. Budget 1,500-2,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Hofsós pool is open year-round but confirm winter hours before visiting. The drive along Route 76 is scenic but can be icy — drive slowly and check road.is. Fuel up in Siglufjörður before departing as petrol stations are sparse.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Akureyri, Iceland's second-largest city, approximately 1 hour and 15 minutes southeast of Siglufjörður via the Ólafsfjörður tunnel. Explore the compact town centre — walk up to Akureyrarkirkja, the iconic church designed by Guðjón Samúelsson, which offers panoramic views over the fjord.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — the world's most northerly botanical garden, free to enter. In January it is a serene snow-covered landscape. Then browse the small independent shops along Hafnarstræti, Akureyri's main street. Visit the Akureyri Art Museum (Listasafnið á Akureyri) — entry around 1,500 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður before road conditions deteriorate after dark. Alternatively, if budget allows, consider staying one night in Akureyri at a guesthouse to explore more tomorrow morning.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Akureyri has a Bonus supermarket — stock up on supplies and eat a packed lunch in the car or at a park bench. Budget 1,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Bautinn restaurant in Akureyri offers traditional Icelandic fish and lamb dishes at relatively affordable prices — around 3,000-4,000 ISK for a main course. Or grab a hot dog from a petrol station for 500 ISK — an Icelandic institution.

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is a great place to stock up on groceries at Bonus (the cheapest supermarket chain in Iceland). The tunnels connecting Siglufjörður and Akureyri are single-lane in sections — follow the passing place rules carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the Tröllaskagi Peninsula scenic route — head south from Siglufjörður along Route 82 through Ólafsfjörður and along the dramatic mountain coastline. Stop at viewpoints overlooking the fjords and snow-capped peaks. This is one of Iceland's most spectacular winter drives.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the small village of Dalvík, approximately 1 hour from Siglufjörður. Explore the Hvoll Museum (Byggðasafnið Hvoll), a quirky local museum featuring a giant — a real Icelandic man who stood 2.34 metres tall. Entry is around 1,000 ISK. Walk along the Dalvík harbour and look for eider ducks and other seabirds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Northern Lights watch from the hotel or the dark hillside above town. January typically offers 15-20 nights of potential aurora activity in northern Iceland.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at a scenic fjord viewpoint along Route 82.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hotel — cook a hearty stew using lamb or fish bought from Akureyri Bonus. Budget 1,500-2,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Route 82 along the Tröllaskagi Peninsula is stunning but can be challenging in winter. Check road.is before departing. Some sections may require 4WD. The peninsula is known for extreme weather — be prepared to turn back if conditions worsen.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Grettislaug hot spring pool near Sauðárkrókur, approximately 1.5 hours south of Siglufjörður via Route 75. This is a small, rustic geothermal pool right on the coast of Skagafjörður, named after the medieval saga hero Grettir the Strong. Entry is around 1,000 ISK. Soaking in a hot spring while surrounded by snow and sea is a quintessential Icelandic winter experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sauðárkrókur town — the largest settlement in Skagafjörður. Visit the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum (Byggðasafn Skagfirðinga) to learn about the region's horse-breeding and farming heritage. Entry around 1,500 ISK. Browse the small town and grab supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Aurora watch from the harbour — the fjord reflects the aurora beautifully on calm nights.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel.
meals.lunch: Eat at a petrol station café in Sauðárkrókur — Icelandic petrol stations (N1, Orkan) serve surprisingly good and affordable hot food like lamb soup and sandwiches. Budget 1,500-2,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hotel. Budget 1,500 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Grettislaug is a very rustic pool — bring your own towel and change in a basic wooden hut. The pool is small and intimate. The drive via Route 75 along Skagafjörður is beautiful. Confirm Grettislaug is accessible in winter as the access road can be snowed over.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Siglufjörður. Sleep in and enjoy a slow morning. Walk along the harbour in the brief morning light and photograph the colourful fishing boats against the snow-covered mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Siglufjörður Folk Music Centre (Þjóðlagasetur) if open — a small museum dedicated to Icelandic folk music traditions. Alternatively, spend the afternoon reading, journalling, or relaxing at the hotel. Take a short snowshoe walk (if snowshoes are available to rent locally) on the lower mountain slopes above town.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated Northern Lights evening — check the aurora forecast carefully and plan to be outside from 21:00 to 01:00 if conditions are favourable. Drive a few kilometres out of town on Route 76 to escape any residual light pollution. Bring a thermos of hot chocolate.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a proper breakfast at Kaffi Rauðka — eggs, toast, and coffee. Budget 2,000 ISK.
meals.lunch: Self-catered at hotel.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hotel — make a traditional Icelandic skyr parfait for dessert. Budget 1,500 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: A rest day is important on a 13-day trip, especially in harsh winter conditions. Use this day to do laundry, recharge camera batteries, and review photos. The aurora forecast website en.vedur.is updates every few hours.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Varmahlíð in Skagafjörður valley, approximately 1.5 hours south. Visit the Víðimýrarkirkja turf church — one of Iceland's best-preserved traditional turf churches, dating to 1834. It is a National Monument and free to view from outside. The snow-covered turf roof is extraordinarily photogenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Skagafjörður valley — drive along Route 1 and take in the wide, flat valley floor surrounded by dramatic mountains. Stop at the Glaumbaer turf farm museum (Glaumbær) — a beautifully preserved 18th-century turf farmstead. Winter hours may be limited but the exterior is always accessible. Entry around 2,000 ISK if open.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Aurora watch if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Glaumbaer or in the car with a fjord view.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hotel. Budget 1,500-2,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbaer museum has reduced winter hours — check their website before visiting. The Skagafjörður valley is famous for Icelandic horse breeding — you may see herds of horses in the snowy fields, which is a magical sight.

day_by_day.morning: Drive back toward Akureyri and visit the Goðafoss waterfall, approximately 50 minutes east of Akureyri on Route 1. One of Iceland's most famous waterfalls, Goðafoss (Waterfall of the Gods) is spectacular in winter when ice formations build up around the edges. Free to visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Mývatn area, approximately 1 hour east of Goðafoss. Visit the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a geothermal lagoon similar to the Blue Lagoon but far less crowded and much cheaper at around 5,500 ISK. Soak in the milky blue silica-rich water surrounded by volcanic landscape and steam.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Akureyri or Siglufjörður. If returning to Siglufjörður, the drive is approximately 2 hours — plan to arrive before 20:00. Aurora watch on the return journey — pull over safely on a dark stretch of road if the lights appear.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before early departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Goðafoss — the waterfall has a small visitor area.
meals.dinner: Gamli Bærinn restaurant near Mývatn offers hearty local food — lamb soup and rye bread. Budget 2,500-3,500 ISK. Or self-cater on return.

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — approximately 4-5 hours total. Start early to make the most of the limited daylight. Mývatn Nature Baths are open year-round and are significantly cheaper than the Blue Lagoon. Book online in advance to guarantee entry. The road between Akureyri and Mývatn (Route 1) is generally well-maintained in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south from Siglufjörður toward the Snæfellsnes Peninsula — a long driving day of approximately 4-5 hours via Akureyri and Route 1 west. This is a repositioning day to explore a new region. Stop at Bifröst or Borgarnes for a break and fuel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive on the Snæfellsnes Peninsula. Visit Kirkjufell mountain near Grundarfjörður — one of Iceland's most photographed mountains, especially dramatic in winter snow. Walk to the Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall viewpoint (free). The mountain and waterfall together create an iconic Icelandic scene.
day_by_day.afternoon_note: Note: This is a very long day. Consider breaking the journey with a night in Akureyri or Borgarnes if budget allows, or commit to the full drive.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into budget accommodation near Grundarfjörður or Stykkishólmur. Aurora watch from the Snæfellsnes coast — the peninsula juts into the Atlantic and offers wide, dark skies.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before early departure.
meals.lunch: Petrol station stop in Borgarnes — N1 or Orkan café for lamb soup. Budget 1,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at new accommodation or a local guesthouse dinner. Budget 2,000-3,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest driving day of the trip at approximately 4-5 hours. Alternatively, skip Snæfellsnes and spend more time exploring the north. If staying on Snæfellsnes, book accommodation in advance as options are limited in winter. Grundarfjörður Hostel or Stykkishólmur guesthouses offer budget options around 8,000-12,000 ISK per night.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Snæfellsjökull National Park — drive the southern coast of the peninsula. Visit Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach, where the rusted remains of a British trawler lie scattered among the volcanic rocks. Free to visit. Walk to the lifting stones (Aflraunasteinar) used historically to test the strength of fishermen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Arnarstapi and Hellnar — two small coastal villages connected by a dramatic 2.5 km coastal walk along basalt cliffs, sea arches, and bird colonies. The walk is free and one of the most beautiful short hikes in Iceland. Visit the Snæfellsjökull glacier viewpoint — the glacier inspired Jules Verne's Journey to the Centre of the Earth.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Reykjavik (approximately 2 hours) or stay another night on Snæfellsnes. If returning to Reykjavik, check into a budget hostel such as Kex Hostel or Loft Hostel (dorm beds from 5,000-7,000 ISK). Aurora watch from Reykjavik outskirts.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Djúpalónssandur beach.
meals.dinner: Reykjavik has many budget options — Hlöllabátar submarine sandwich shop offers large, filling sandwiches for around 1,500-2,000 ISK. Or cook at the hostel kitchen.

day_by_day.notes: The coastal walk between Arnarstapi and Hellnar is moderately easy but can be icy in January — wear grip footwear. Snæfellsjökull glacier tours are available but expensive (15,000-20,000 ISK) — skip for budget travel. The peninsula is very exposed to Atlantic weather — dress in full waterproofs.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Reykjavik on a budget. Walk the Laugavegur shopping street and Skólavörðustígur. Visit Hallgrímskirkja church — the exterior is free, the tower lift costs 1,000 ISK and offers panoramic city views. Visit the Sun Voyager sculpture (Sólfar) on the harbour front — free and iconic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjavik Flea Market (Kolaportið) if it is a weekend — a beloved local institution selling second-hand goods, Icelandic woolens, and traditional food like hákarl (fermented shark) and dried fish. Entry is free. Alternatively, visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — an underground museum built around a Viking-age longhouse. Entry around 2,200 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights attempt — take a free city bus or walk to Öskjuhlíð hill (Perlan area) or drive to the Reykjanes Peninsula for darker skies. Many free aurora tours depart from Reykjavik city centre — join a group for safety and local knowledge.

meals.breakfast: Reykjavik Roasters café — excellent coffee and pastries. Budget 1,500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — the famous Reykjavik hot dog stand near the harbour. A hot dog costs around 600 ISK. An absolute must-do.
meals.dinner: Sægreifinn (Sea Baron) on the harbour — famous for lobster soup (humarsúpa) at around 1,800 ISK per bowl. One of Reykjavik's best budget dining experiences.

day_by_day.notes: Reykjavik is expensive — stick to self-catering and street food to manage costs. The city's geothermal swimming pools (Sundhöll Reykjavíkur, Laugardalslaug) are excellent value at around 1,000 ISK and are used daily by locals. A swim at a city pool is a wonderful cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. If time allows before departure, visit the Blue Lagoon — book in advance as it sells out. The Comfort package starts at around 12,000 ISK. Alternatively, save money and visit the Reykjanes Peninsula geothermal area (Gunnuhver mud pools and Reykjanes lighthouse) for free — dramatic volcanic landscapes just 20 minutes from Keflavik Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Keflavik International Airport. Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security. Browse the duty-free shop for last-minute Icelandic chocolate, skyr, and Brennivín schnapps at airport prices.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of Northern Lights, hot springs, volcanic landscapes, and Arctic winter magic.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hostel or a final Icelandic breakfast of skyr, rye bread, and smoked salmon. Budget 1,500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Grab a meal at Keflavik Airport — prices are high so budget 2,500-3,500 ISK for a simple meal, or eat before arriving at the airport.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport food.

day_by_day.notes: Check out of Reykjavik accommodation by 11:00 typically. Store luggage at the BSI bus terminal if needed for a few hours. The Flybus from BSI to Keflavik Airport takes 45 minutes and costs around 3,500 ISK — book in advance. Do not leave Iceland without trying skyr one last time. Total estimated daily budget excluding accommodation: 5,000-8,000 ISK per day (approximately €35-55 EUR) if self-catering and avoiding tourist traps.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs, collect luggage, and pick up pre-booked rental car (4WD essential for winter Iceland). Grab a coffee and light breakfast at the airport café before beginning the long drive north to Siglufjörður (~5.5 hours in winter conditions). Drive through the Hvalfjörður tunnel and along the Ringroad, stopping briefly at Borgarnes for fuel and a stretch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the scenic drive north through Varmahlíð and into the Tröllaskagi peninsula. The dramatic mountain scenery and fjords become increasingly striking. Arrive in Siglufjörður in the early afternoon. Check in to Hotel Siglunes, freshen up, and take a short walk along the harbour to get oriented in this charming fishing village.
day_by_day.evening: Settle in for a quiet first evening. Have dinner at the hotel restaurant or nearby Hannes Boy restaurant, one of Siglufjörður's most beloved spots. Afterwards, step outside to check for northern lights — Siglufjörður's remote location and minimal light pollution make it an excellent aurora-watching spot. Wrap up warm and scan the sky before an early bedtime to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Airport café at Keflavík — coffee, skyr yoghurt, and a pastry (~1,500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Roadside stop in Borgarnes — Borgarnes Settlement Center café for soup and bread (~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy restaurant in Siglufjörður — fresh fish of the day or lamb soup (~4,500–6,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Drive carefully — January roads in northern Iceland can be icy and subject to closures. Check road.is before and during the drive. The Héðinsfjörður tunnel and Strákagöng tunnel are used to access Siglufjörður. Fuel up whenever possible as stations are sparse in the north.

day_by_day.morning: After a good rest, enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Then visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) right in Siglufjörður — one of Iceland's finest regional museums, telling the story of the town's herring boom era. Allow 1.5–2 hours to explore the three restored warehouses and fascinating exhibits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the short distance to Hofsós (about 45 minutes south along the peninsula) to visit the stunning infinity-edge geothermal swimming pool perched above the fjord — one of Iceland's most scenic public pools. Soak in the warm water while gazing out over Skagafjörður. Return to Siglufjörður in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights watch from the hillside above town or the harbour pier. The Tröllaskagi peninsula offers superb dark skies. Download the Vedur aurora forecast app and head out if activity is predicted above level 3. Dress in full winter layers — hat, gloves, thermal base layers, and waterproof outer shell.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast buffet — included or ~2,000 ISK, featuring skyr, eggs, smoked salmon, and rye bread
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or light snack from Krónan supermarket in Siglufjörður before heading to Hofsós
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — cosy café-restaurant with homemade soups, sandwiches, and daily specials (~3,500–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Hofsós pool entry is approximately 1,000 ISK. Bring your own towel or rent one on-site. The pool may have limited winter hours — check ahead. The drive between Siglufjörður and Hofsós is scenic but can be icy; allow extra time.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south to Akureyri, Iceland's second-largest city (~1.5 hours from Siglufjörður). Explore the charming town centre — visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hill, stroll the pedestrian Hafnarstræti street, and browse local shops. Stop at Bláa Kannan café for a warm drink.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — even in winter the grounds are peaceful and the greenhouse is open. Then head to the Akureyri Art Museum or the Nonni House museum for cultural depth. Alternatively, visit the local geothermal swimming pool (Sundlaug Akureyrar) — one of the best in Iceland with multiple hot pots and slides.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Akureyri before the drive back to Siglufjörður. Akureyri has the best dining options in the north. Return to the hotel and check aurora forecasts for a late-night sky watch if conditions are favourable.

meals.breakfast: Bláa Kannan café in Akureyri — famous for its cosy atmosphere, coffee, and fresh pastries (~1,800 ISK)
meals.lunch: Strikið restaurant or Rub23 in Akureyri — mid-range lunch menu with local fish and lamb options (~3,000–4,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Greifinn restaurant in Akureyri — popular local favourite with pizza, pasta, and Icelandic mains at reasonable prices (~4,000–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is a worthwhile day trip from Siglufjörður. The Sundlaug Akureyrar pool entry is ~1,000 ISK. Parking in Akureyri town centre is free for the first hour. Return drive in darkness — use caution on the mountain roads.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the immediate surroundings of Siglufjörður on foot. Walk the harbour front and up into the residential streets to appreciate the colourful wooden houses. Visit the small but charming Folk Music Centre (Þjóðlagasetur) which celebrates Icelandic folk music traditions. The town is compact and very walkable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive through the Héðinsfjörður tunnel to the neighbouring abandoned fjord of Héðinsfjörður — a hauntingly beautiful and completely uninhabited valley. Walk around the old farmstead ruins and take in the dramatic mountain scenery. Return through the tunnel and drive to Ólafsfjörður (15 minutes south) for a look at another traditional fishing village.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting — this is a self-guided evening. Drive out of town along the fjord road away from any light sources. Park safely and wait for the aurora. January is statistically one of the best months for northern lights in Iceland due to long dark nights. Bring a thermos of hot chocolate and a tripod for photography.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — full Icelandic breakfast with eggs, skyr, and smoked fish
meals.lunch: Packed lunch prepared from supermarket supplies — rye bread, smoked lamb, cheese, and fruit
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes restaurant — try the catch of the day or Icelandic lamb with root vegetables (~4,500–6,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Héðinsfjörður is accessible via a tunnel but the valley itself requires walking on uneven terrain — wear sturdy waterproof boots. The area is completely isolated so ensure your phone is charged and you have emergency supplies in the car.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east along Route 1 toward Lake Mývatn (~2 hours from Siglufjörður via Akureyri). This geothermally active region is one of Iceland's most extraordinary landscapes. Begin at the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a less-crowded alternative to the Blue Lagoon with stunning views over the volcanic landscape. Soak in the silica-rich geothermal waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mývatn area's volcanic wonders. Visit the Dimmuborgir lava field — a surreal landscape of twisted lava formations and caves. Walk the marked trails through the eerie rock pillars. Then visit the Skútustaðagígar pseudo-craters — a UNESCO-listed area of explosion craters formed when lava flowed over wetlands.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Akureyri and then north to Siglufjörður, arriving by early evening. The long drive back gives you time to reflect on the day's extraordinary geology. Check aurora forecasts and, if conditions are good, stop at a dark spot on the way home for a northern lights viewing opportunity.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — pack extra snacks for the road
meals.lunch: Gamli Bærinn restaurant near Mývatn — traditional Icelandic lamb soup and bread in a cosy farmhouse setting (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka or hotel restaurant in Siglufjörður upon return (~3,500–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Mývatn Nature Baths entry is approximately 6,500 ISK — book online in advance. The drive to Mývatn is long but the road is generally well-maintained. Allow extra time for winter driving conditions. Dimmuborgir trails may be icy — use microspikes if available.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning in Siglufjörður. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and spend time in the hotel. If weather permits, take a gentle hike up the hillside above town for panoramic views of the fjord and surrounding mountains. The ski area above Siglufjörður (Skíðasvæðið) may have limited winter operations — check if any lifts are running for a scenic ride up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Siglufjörður swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) — a local geothermal pool with hot pots, perfect for warming up on a cold January afternoon. Afterwards, explore the town's small independent shops and pick up local souvenirs — Icelandic wool products, local jams, and herring-themed gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated northern lights evening. Book a guided Northern Lights Hunting Tour departing from Akureyri or Siglufjörður area — a local guide will drive you to the best viewing spots based on real-time aurora forecasts and cloud cover. The guided experience increases your chances significantly and includes photography tips.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — leisurely breakfast with fresh bread, cold cuts, and Icelandic dairy
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Kaffi Rauðka — homemade cake, soup, and coffee (~2,000–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy restaurant — splurge slightly on a three-course dinner featuring local Arctic char or lamb (~6,000–8,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The local swimming pool is an authentic Icelandic experience and costs only ~1,000 ISK. Northern lights tours from the Akureyri area typically cost 8,000–12,000 ISK per person — book in advance through local operators like Arctic Adventures or local Akureyri tour companies.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west to the Skagafjörður valley (~1 hour from Siglufjörður). This region is famous for Icelandic horse breeding. Visit a local horse farm for a short guided tour or horse riding experience — even a 1-hour winter ride through the snowy landscape is magical. The Icelandic horse is uniquely suited to winter terrain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Varmahlíð and visit the Glaumbær turf farm museum — one of Iceland's best-preserved historical turf farmsteads, offering a fascinating glimpse into traditional Icelandic rural life. The adjacent Ásgeirsstaðir café serves excellent homemade cakes and coffee. Return to Siglufjörður via the scenic coastal route.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening at the hotel. Review photos from the week, plan the upcoming days, and enjoy a relaxed dinner. If the sky is clear, take a short walk to the harbour for aurora watching — no guide needed on a clear night with good forecast.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fuel up before the day's driving
meals.lunch: Ásgeirsstaðir café at Glaumbær — homemade Icelandic pancakes (pönnukökur) with cream and jam, coffee (~1,500–2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes restaurant — Icelandic fish stew or lamb chops with seasonal vegetables (~4,500–6,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Horse riding tours in Skagafjörður cost approximately 8,000–12,000 ISK per person for a 1-hour ride. Book ahead through Hestur.is or local farms. Glaumbær museum entry is ~2,000 ISK. The turf farm may have limited winter hours — confirm before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the long drive south toward the Golden Circle area (~5–6 hours from Siglufjörður). This is a travel day, so depart early after breakfast. Drive south along Route 1 through Akureyri and into the interior highlands approach. Stop at Goðafoss waterfall on the way — one of Iceland's most beautiful and accessible waterfalls, especially dramatic in winter with ice formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south, stopping at Geysir geothermal area in the Golden Circle. Watch the famous Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes, shooting boiling water 20–30 metres into the air. Walk the geothermal field and observe the bubbling mud pools and steaming vents. Check in to a mid-range guesthouse or hotel in the Selfoss/Flúðir area for the next two nights.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and a small geyser. Soak under the stars in this intimate, less-commercialised setting. The experience is magical on a clear winter night.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast in Siglufjörður before departure
meals.lunch: Geysir Center café — lamb soup and fresh bread at the visitor centre (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Minilik Ethiopian restaurant in Selfoss or Tryggvaskáli restaurant — mid-range dinner in a historic building (~4,000–6,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon entry is approximately 3,500 ISK — book online in advance as it can sell out. The drive from Siglufjörður to the Golden Circle is long; check road conditions on road.is before departing. Goðafoss is accessible directly from Route 1 with a short walk to the viewpoint.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet and where Iceland's first parliament was established in 930 AD. Walk the Almannagjá rift valley, visit the Öxará river, and take in the extraordinary geological and historical significance of this place.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Gullfoss waterfall — the iconic 'Golden Falls' where the Hvítá river plunges into a dramatic canyon. In winter, the falls are often partially frozen and surrounded by ice formations, making for spectacular photography. Afterwards, visit the Kerið volcanic crater lake — a vivid red and green crater with a turquoise lake at its centre.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Selfoss/Flúðir area. If aurora forecast is favourable, drive to a dark spot near Þingvellir or along the Þingvallavatn lake shore for northern lights viewing — the lake reflection can create stunning aurora displays. Otherwise, enjoy a relaxed dinner and early night.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local bakery in Selfoss — fresh pastries and coffee (~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.lunch: Gullfoss Café at the waterfall — hot lamb soup and coffee to warm up (~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Selfoss town restaurant — Kaffi Krús or similar mid-range option with Icelandic fish and meat dishes (~4,000–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Þingvellir National Park is free to enter; parking costs ~750 ISK. Kerið crater entry is ~400 ISK. Gullfoss is free. The Golden Circle can be busy even in winter — arrive at each site early to beat tour buses. Dress in full winter gear as wind chill at Gullfoss can be extreme.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Reykjanes Peninsula for the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa experience — one of Iceland's most iconic attractions. Pre-booked entry includes access to the milky-blue silica-rich waters, a silica mud mask, and use of facilities. Arrive for the first morning slot to enjoy it before crowds build. The contrast of steaming blue water against the black lava field is unforgettable.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Blue Lagoon, explore the Reykjanes Peninsula's raw volcanic landscape. Visit the Bridge Between Continents — a small footbridge spanning the rift between the North American and Eurasian plates. Drive to Reykjanesviti lighthouse and the Gunnuhver hot spring area with its powerful steam vents and boiling mud pools.
day_by_day.evening: Drive into Reykjavík (45 minutes from Reykjanes) and check in to a mid-range hotel or guesthouse in the city centre for the final nights. Explore the Laugavegur shopping street and enjoy dinner in the capital. The city's vibrant food scene offers excellent options at every price point.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at guesthouse before departing for Blue Lagoon — the lagoon experience includes a drink
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon LAVA Restaurant or the lagoon's in-water drink service — budget for ~3,000–5,000 ISK for food at the lagoon
meals.dinner: Reykjavík — Sægreifinn (Sea Baron) on the harbour — famous for lobster soup and grilled fish skewers at very reasonable prices (~3,000–4,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon must be booked well in advance — January slots sell out. Comfort package costs approximately 14,990 ISK. Arrive 15 minutes before your slot. The lagoon provides towels and a locker. Silica mud masks are included. Remove all jewellery before entering as the minerals can damage metal.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Reykjavík's highlights. Visit Hallgrímskirkja church — take the lift to the top of the tower for panoramic city views. Walk to the Harpa Concert Hall on the harbour for its stunning geometric glass architecture. Stroll along the Tjörnin lake and through the old town streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) for a comprehensive overview of Icelandic history and culture — excellent exhibits covering the Viking settlement to modern times. Alternatively, visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) built around actual Viking-age ruins discovered beneath the city. Browse the Kolaportið flea market if it's open (weekends only).
day_by_day.evening: Join a Northern Lights Hunting Tour departing from Reykjavík. Professional guides monitor aurora forecasts in real time and drive participants to the best viewing locations outside the city. Tours typically last 3–4 hours and include hot chocolate. This is your best guided aurora opportunity of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Reykjavík hotel breakfast or Brauð & Co bakery — Iceland's best sourdough bread and pastries (~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.lunch: Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — traditional Icelandic food including hákarl (fermented shark), rye bread ice cream, and lamb (~2,500–4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Pre-tour dinner at Snaps Bistro Bar — French-Icelandic fusion at mid-range prices (~5,000–7,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Hallgrímskirkja tower lift costs ~1,000 ISK. National Museum entry is ~2,500 ISK. Northern lights tours from Reykjavík cost approximately 8,000–12,000 ISK — book through Reykjavík Excursions, Arctic Adventures, or similar operators. Tours are weather-dependent and reputable companies offer free rebooking if conditions are poor.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure at Þingvellir National Park. This world-renowned dive site offers visibility of over 100 metres in glacially filtered water. Snorkelling between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Dry suits are provided — no prior diving experience needed for snorkelling. Depart Reykjavík early for the 45-minute drive.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Silfra experience, warm up with hot chocolate provided by the tour operator. Spend additional time exploring Þingvellir National Park on foot — the Öxará river canyon and Almannagjá rift are beautiful in winter light. Return to Reykjavík by mid-afternoon for some final souvenir shopping on Laugavegur.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Iceland. Enjoy a special dinner at one of Reykjavík's celebrated restaurants. Afterwards, take a final walk along the harbour and Sæbraut coastal road — if the aurora is active, the northern waterfront offers good dark-sky views away from the brightest city lights.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departing for Silfra — the tour requires an early start
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snack at Þingvellir visitor centre café — soup and coffee (~2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) — upscale Icelandic ingredients cooked over lava stone grill; splurge for the final night (~8,000–12,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkelling tours cost approximately 18,000–22,000 ISK per person — book well in advance through DIVE.IS or Arctic Adventures. Water temperature is 2–4°C year-round but dry suits keep you warm. You must be able to swim. Minimum age is typically 12. Bring a swimsuit to wear under the dry suit.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a leisurely last breakfast in Reykjavík. Take a final walk to the Sun Voyager sculpture (Sólfar) on the harbour — a beautiful Viking ship sculpture that makes for excellent morning photography. Visit a local shop for any last-minute souvenirs — Icelandic wool lopapeysa sweaters, Brennivín schnapps, or local chocolate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Keflavík International Airport (45 minutes from Reykjavík city centre). Return the rental car — allow at least 30 minutes for the return process. Check in and clear security with time to spare. Browse the duty-free shops at the airport — Icelandic products are often cheaper here than in the city.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavík. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days in Iceland — northern lights, geothermal pools, volcanic landscapes, and the unique culture of this remarkable island nation.

meals.breakfast: Final Reykjavík breakfast — Sandholt Bakery on Laugavegur for exceptional pastries, open sandwiches, and coffee (~2,000–2,500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café at Keflavík — Icelandic fish and chips or a burger (~3,000–4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Return the rental car with a full tank of fuel — there is a petrol station near the airport. Allow extra time at the airport in January as winter weather can cause delays. Keflavík airport has good duty-free shopping including Icelandic wool products, spirits, and cosmetics. The Blue Lagoon is located between Reykjavík and the airport — a final soak is possible if your flight departs in the evening and you book the earliest morning slot.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the aurora borealis dancing across the sky. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind this natural phenomenon while capturing stunning photographs.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and swim-up bars while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the main lagoon, towel rental, and one silica mud mask.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. The surreal blue and green hues of the water make this one of the most unique natural experiences on Earth, guided by certified instructors.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a peaceful soak amid stunning Icelandic countryside.

experiences.name: Skaftafell Glacier Hike on Vatnajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier with an expert guide. Explore stunning ice formations, deep blue crevasses, and ash layers from ancient volcanic eruptions. The hike offers breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding black sand plains and mountain peaks.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Transfer via private luxury vehicle (pre-arranged chauffeur service) toward Reykjavik for a brief orientation stop before beginning the long scenic drive north to Siglufjörður. The drive is approximately 5–6 hours; enjoy the dramatic winter landscapes of the Icelandic highlands en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop in Akureyri (Iceland's 'Capital of the North') for a leisurely exploration of the charming town center, the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church overlooking the fjord, and a warm-up coffee break at a local café. Continue the final 45-minute scenic drive along the Tröllaskagi peninsula to Siglufjörður, arriving at Hotel Siglunes in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to Hotel Siglunes and settle into your premium room with fjord views. After freshening up, enjoy a welcome dinner at the hotel's acclaimed restaurant featuring locally sourced Arctic char, lamb, and seasonal Icelandic ingredients paired with fine Scandinavian wines.

meals.breakfast: Light refreshments at Keflavík Airport lounge (Icelandair Saga Lounge) before departure or en route
meals.lunch: Lunch at Rub23 in Akureyri — an award-winning restaurant known for its fresh Arctic seafood and sushi with a Nordic twist
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Siglunes restaurant — intimate fine dining with panoramic fjord views; try the pan-seared Arctic char with dill cream and roasted root vegetables

day_by_day.notes: Given the very early arrival and long transfer, keep Day 1 relaxed. Pre-arrange the private chauffeur transfer from Keflavík to Siglufjörður (approx. 5.5–6 hrs). January daylight in Siglufjörður is extremely limited (roughly 5 hours), so the drive will be partly in darkness — embrace the dramatic atmosphere. Check aurora forecast upon arrival; if conditions are favorable, step outside the hotel after dinner for a spontaneous northern lights viewing from the fjord.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely breakfast at the hotel, take a guided snowshoe walk through the snow-covered mountains surrounding Siglufjörður. The town is nestled in one of Iceland's most dramatic fjords and offers stunning winter scenery. A local guide will lead you through pristine snowfields with views of the frozen harbor below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's finest regional museums — to learn about Siglufjörður's fascinating history as the herring capital of the North Atlantic. Afterward, explore the colorful village on foot and visit local artisan shops. Warm up with a traditional Icelandic hot chocolate at Kaffi Rauðka.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour: Join a guided evening excursion into the mountains above Siglufjörður, far from any light pollution, for optimal aurora borealis viewing. Your expert guide will monitor solar activity and cloud cover to find the best vantage point. Wrap up in provided thermal suits and enjoy hot cocoa under the dancing lights.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — skyr with berries, smoked salmon, rye bread, eggs, and Icelandic cheeses
meals.lunch: Lunch at Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — cozy café with homemade soups, open-faced sandwiches, and fresh pastries
meals.dinner: Return to Hotel Siglunes for a premium dinner; try the slow-braised Icelandic lamb shank with root vegetable purée and red wine reduction

day_by_day.notes: Aurora activity is highly dependent on clear skies and solar conditions. January is statistically one of the best months for northern lights in northern Iceland. The Tröllaskagi peninsula's remote location makes it ideal for aurora hunting. Dress in multiple thermal layers; the hotel can provide or recommend gear rental.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the scenic Tröllaskagi peninsula route (Route 76) south toward Hofsós, stopping at dramatic coastal viewpoints overlooking frozen fjords and snow-capped peaks. Visit the Hofsós Infinity Pool — a geothermal swimming pool dramatically perched on the edge of Skagafjörður fjord, offering one of Iceland's most breathtaking bathing experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Sauðárkrókur, the largest town in Skagafjörður, for a visit to the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum. Explore the region's Viking-age history and horse culture (Skagafjörður is famous for Icelandic horses). If conditions allow, arrange a private winter horseback riding experience on the legendary Icelandic horse breed through snowy farmland.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður via the scenic mountain tunnel route. Enjoy a relaxed evening at Hotel Siglunes with a private in-room hot tub session (if available) or unwind in the hotel's lounge with a glass of Icelandic craft beer or aquavit while watching for aurora activity through the panoramic windows.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ólafsfjörður's local restaurant en route — fresh fish soup and Icelandic bread
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Siglunes — pan-seared cod with langoustine bisque and seasonal vegetables, paired with a crisp Chablis

day_by_day.notes: The Hofsós Infinity Pool is a hidden gem and far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon. Bring a swimsuit and towel (or rent on-site). The drive along Route 76 is spectacular but can be icy in January — ensure the rental or chauffeur vehicle has winter tires and 4WD. Check road conditions at road.is before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Morning ice fishing excursion on one of the frozen lakes near Siglufjörður with a local guide. Drill through the ice and fish for Arctic char and trout in a truly authentic Icelandic winter experience. The guide will provide all equipment and share traditional techniques passed down through generations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Siglufjörður Folk Music Center and explore the town's rich musical heritage. Afterward, take a private photography tour of the fjord with a local professional photographer who will guide you to the best vantage points for capturing the dramatic winter light, snow-covered rooftops, and colorful harbor buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour (second attempt on a different night for better odds): Head to a high-altitude viewpoint above the fjord with your guide. If aurora activity is strong, this elevated position offers a 360-degree panoramic view of the dancing lights reflected in the fjord below. Return to the hotel for a nightcap by the fireplace.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch prepared by the hotel for the ice fishing excursion — thermos of hot soup, smoked lamb sandwiches, and Icelandic cookies
meals.dinner: Special chef's tasting menu at Hotel Siglunes — a curated 4-course meal showcasing the finest local ingredients: langoustine, reindeer, skyr dessert, and Icelandic cheese board

day_by_day.notes: Ice fishing requires warm, waterproof clothing and patience — but it is an incredibly rewarding and authentic experience. The photography tour is best scheduled around the brief golden-hour window (approximately 11:30 AM–1:30 PM in January) when the low sun casts extraordinary warm light across the fjord.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siglufjörður early and drive east along the stunning Eyjafjörður fjord toward Akureyri (approx. 1 hour). Stop at Laufás, a beautifully preserved 19th-century turf farmhouse museum, for a glimpse into traditional Icelandic rural life. Continue into Akureyri for a morning of exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — the world's northernmost botanical garden — and the Akureyri Art Museum. Explore the charming pedestrian shopping street, Hafnarstræti, browsing Icelandic design boutiques and wool shops. Treat yourself to a traditional Icelandic pastry (kleina) at a local bakery.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a premium dinner at one of Akureyri's finest restaurants before returning to Siglufjörður. Alternatively, if aurora conditions are exceptional, stop at a dark-sky location along the Eyjafjörður fjord for impromptu northern lights viewing on the drive back.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Strikið Restaurant in Akureyri — rooftop dining with panoramic fjord views; known for excellent steaks and fresh seafood
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rub23 in Akureyri (if not visited on Day 1) or Greifinn Restaurant — cozy atmosphere with excellent lamb and fish dishes

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is a wonderful base for day trips and offers a surprising amount of culture and cuisine for a small Arctic city. The drive between Siglufjörður and Akureyri through the Héðinsfjörður tunnel is dramatic and scenic. Allow extra time for road conditions in January.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Mývatn region (approx. 1.5 hours east of Akureyri). Begin with a visit to the extraordinary Mývatn Nature Baths — a premium geothermal lagoon set amid volcanic landscapes, often called the 'Blue Lagoon of the North' but far more serene and less crowded. Soak in the mineral-rich, silica-blue waters with views of the surrounding lava fields.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the surreal volcanic landscape around Lake Mývatn: visit the Dimmuborgir lava formations (dramatic black lava pillars and caves), the Hverfjall tephra crater, and the Námaskarð geothermal area with its bubbling mud pools and steaming fumaroles. The otherworldly landscape is particularly dramatic under a winter sky.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mývatn Nature Baths for a twilight soak as darkness falls — the combination of steaming geothermal waters, volcanic scenery, and potential aurora activity overhead is truly magical. Drive back to Siglufjörður for a late dinner at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Vogafjós Farm Resort near Mývatn — famous for its farm-to-table dining; try the geothermally baked rye bread with smoked trout and fresh dairy products from their own cows
meals.dinner: Late dinner at Hotel Siglunes — warm lamb stew with Icelandic herbs and freshly baked bread, followed by skyr panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: The Mývatn Nature Baths are significantly less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and offer a more authentic, premium experience. Book in advance. The Námaskarð geothermal area is free to visit and absolutely spectacular — the sulfurous steam and colorful mineral deposits are unlike anything else in Iceland. Dress in waterproof layers as the geothermal steam can dampen clothing.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at Hotel Siglunes. Enjoy a slow breakfast and take a leisurely walk along the Siglufjörður harbor waterfront, watching local fishing boats and enjoying the crisp Arctic air. Visit the town's small but charming local swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) — a beloved community geothermal pool — for a relaxing morning soak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a private guided snowmobile tour through the mountains above Siglufjörður. The Tröllaskagi peninsula offers some of Iceland's best snowmobile terrain, with vast snowfields and dramatic ridge-top views across multiple fjords. This is an exhilarating premium experience unique to this region.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a special 'Northern Lights Dinner' at Hotel Siglunes — dine at a table positioned by the panoramic windows with aurora alerts set up on your phone. The hotel staff will notify you if the lights appear so you can step outside immediately. Pair the evening with a premium Icelandic whisky tasting.

meals.breakfast: Extended leisurely breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — full spread with fresh pastries, smoked fish, and Icelandic dairy
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or a local café in Siglufjörður — fish soup and rye bread
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at Hotel Siglunes with wine pairing — grilled reindeer tenderloin with juniper berry sauce, roasted beets, and potato gratin

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally lighter to allow for rest mid-trip. The snowmobile tour requires a valid driver's license and a brief safety briefing. Minimum age and weight restrictions may apply. Book through the hotel concierge in advance. January snowpack in the Tröllaskagi mountains is typically excellent for snowmobiling.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south from Siglufjörður toward the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approx. 4–4.5 hours). This is a travel day with scenic stops. Stop at Borgarnes for a visit to the Settlement Center of Iceland — an excellent museum dedicated to the Viking settlement of Iceland and the Egils Saga.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive on the Snæfellsnes Peninsula and visit Snæfellsjökull National Park. Drive around the dramatic western tip of the peninsula, stopping at the iconic Kirkjufell mountain (Iceland's most photographed peak) and Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall — particularly magical in winter with ice formations. Visit the black sand beach at Djúpalónssandur.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a premium guesthouse or boutique hotel on the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (e.g., Hotel Búðir — one of Iceland's most romantic and remote luxury hotels, set beside a historic black church on a lava field). Enjoy dinner at Hotel Búðir's acclaimed restaurant with views of the glacier.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Settlement Center Restaurant in Borgarnes — excellent lamb soup and traditional Icelandic dishes in a historic setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Búðir Restaurant — one of Iceland's finest dining experiences; try the slow-roasted lamb with wild mushrooms and glacier-fed spring water vegetables

day_by_day.notes: This is a longer driving day — approximately 4–4.5 hours total. Depart Siglufjörður by 8:00 AM to make the most of the limited daylight. The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is often called 'Iceland in Miniature' as it contains glaciers, lava fields, fishing villages, bird cliffs, and hot springs all in one compact area. Hotel Búðir must be booked well in advance — it is one of Iceland's most sought-after luxury properties.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Snæfellsjökull glacier — the mystical glacier that Jules Verne used as the entrance to the Earth's core in 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Join a guided snowcat or snowmobile tour onto the glacier summit for extraordinary panoramic views of the peninsula and, on clear days, Reykjavik across the bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the charming fishing village of Arnarstapi and walk the dramatic coastal path to Hellnar, passing sea arches, basalt columns, and nesting seabirds (even in winter). Stop at the Vatnshellir lava tube cave for a guided underground tour through an 8,000-year-old volcanic tunnel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hotel Búðir for a relaxed evening. If aurora conditions are favorable, the remote location of Hotel Búðir — surrounded by lava fields with zero light pollution — makes it one of Iceland's finest spots for northern lights viewing directly from the hotel grounds. Enjoy a nightcap by the fireplace.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Búðir
meals.lunch: Lunch at Fjöruhúsið Café in Hellnar — a legendary cliffside café known for its homemade soups, cakes, and dramatic ocean views; a true hidden gem
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Búðir — fresh langoustine bisque followed by pan-seared halibut with herb butter and seasonal vegetables

day_by_day.notes: The Snæfellsjökull glacier tour requires advance booking and appropriate weather conditions. The glacier is at 1,446 meters elevation and weather can change rapidly. The coastal walk from Arnarstapi to Hellnar (approx. 2.5 km) is manageable in winter with proper footwear but can be icy — use microspikes. Fjöruhúsið Café is a must-visit and is open year-round.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Snæfellsnes and drive to the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir (approx. 2.5 hours via the Golden Circle route). Arrive for a morning soak in Iceland's oldest swimming pool — a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and steaming geysers. The intimate, rustic atmosphere is far more authentic than the Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle route: visit the famous Geysir geothermal area where the Strokkur geyser erupts every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–30 meters into the air. Then visit the majestic Gullfoss waterfall — partially frozen in January, creating extraordinary ice formations around the cascading water.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Reykjavik (approx. 1.5 hours from Gullfoss) and check in to a premium Reykjavik hotel (e.g., The Retreat at Blue Lagoon or Hotel Borg — an iconic art deco luxury hotel in the heart of the city). Enjoy a sophisticated dinner in Reykjavik's vibrant restaurant scene.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Búðir before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Friðheimar Greenhouse Restaurant in Reykholt — a unique dining experience inside a working tomato greenhouse; famous for its tomato soup and fresh tomato-based menu
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dill Restaurant in Reykjavik — Iceland's only Michelin-starred restaurant, offering a stunning New Nordic tasting menu celebrating Icelandic ingredients and culinary heritage

day_by_day.notes: Dill Restaurant requires advance reservation — book as early as possible, ideally months ahead. The Secret Lagoon is best visited early morning before tour groups arrive. Gullfoss in January is spectacular but the paths can be very icy — wear microspikes. The Golden Circle is Iceland's most popular tourist route but in January crowds are significantly reduced.

day_by_day.morning: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa: Transfer from Reykjavik to the world-famous Blue Lagoon (approx. 45 minutes). Book the premium 'Retreat Spa' experience — the most exclusive offering at the Blue Lagoon, including private changing facilities, in-water floating massage, silica mud mask treatment, algae mask, and access to the exclusive Retreat Lagoon (separate from the main public lagoon). Spend a luxurious morning soaking in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik and explore the city's cultural highlights: visit Hallgrímskirkja church (take the elevator to the top for panoramic city views), the Harpa Concert Hall (a stunning glass structure on the harbor), and the National Museum of Iceland for an overview of Icelandic history from settlement to present day.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour from Reykjavik: Join a premium guided evening tour by super jeep into the Reykjanes Peninsula or toward Þingvellir National Park, away from the city's light pollution. Expert guides monitor aurora forecasts in real time and drive to optimal viewing locations. Return to Reykjavik for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Reykjavik hotel
meals.lunch: Lava Restaurant at the Blue Lagoon — dine in the iconic restaurant built into the lava rock with views over the steaming lagoon; try the langoustine and Icelandic lamb
meals.dinner: Dinner at Grillið Restaurant at Radisson Blu Saga Hotel — Reykjavik's premier rooftop fine dining restaurant with panoramic city views; excellent lamb and seafood

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa experience must be booked well in advance — it sells out months ahead. The premium Retreat package is significantly more expensive than standard entry but offers an incomparably exclusive experience. Bring your own hair care products as the silica-rich water can be harsh on hair. The evening northern lights tour from Reykjavik is less optimal than from Siglufjörður due to more light pollution, but professional guides maximize your chances.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure at Þingvellir National Park (approx. 45 minutes from Reykjavik). Don a dry suit and snorkel (or scuba dive) between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. This UNESCO World Heritage Site offers one of the world's most unique underwater experiences. The water temperature is approximately 2–4°C year-round, but dry suits keep you comfortable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Þingvellir National Park on foot — the site of the world's first parliament (Alþingi, established 930 AD) and a place of profound historical and geological significance. Walk along the dramatic Almannagjá rift valley, visit the Öxará River (partially frozen in January), and take in the vast, silent winter landscape of this sacred Icelandic site.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik for a final evening of luxury dining and exploration. Walk the vibrant Laugavegur shopping street, visit a local design boutique for premium Icelandic souvenirs (Icelandic wool sweaters, lava jewelry, artisan spirits), and enjoy a farewell dinner at one of Reykjavik's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Reykjavik hotel
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch provided by the dive operator or a quick stop at Þingvellir visitor center café — hot soup and sandwiches
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Óx Restaurant in Reykjavik — an ultra-exclusive 12-seat chef's counter restaurant offering an extraordinary tasting menu; one of Iceland's most unique dining experiences (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkeling requires advance booking and a minimum level of swimming ability. No prior diving experience is needed for snorkeling. The water is extremely cold — follow all guide instructions regarding dry suit use. Þingvellir is a deeply significant site in Icelandic culture and history — take time to absorb the atmosphere beyond just the geological features. Óx Restaurant has very limited seating and must be booked months in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at your Reykjavik hotel. If time permits before airport transfer, visit the Reykjavik Flea Market (Kolaportið) for last-minute Icelandic souvenirs, or take a final walk along the Sæbraut coastal path with views of Mount Esja across the bay. Visit the Sun Voyager sculpture (Sólfarið) — a stunning steel Viking ship sculpture on the Reykjavik waterfront — for a memorable final photo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport (approx. 45 minutes from Reykjavik). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and time in the Icelandair Saga Lounge. Depart Iceland with extraordinary memories of aurora-lit fjords, steaming geothermal pools, and the raw, untamed beauty of the Arctic.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days exploring Iceland's most dramatic winter landscapes, from the remote fjords of Siglufjörður to the geothermal wonders of the Golden Circle and the tectonic marvels of Þingvellir.

meals.breakfast: Final full Icelandic breakfast at your Reykjavik hotel — savor every last bite of smoked salmon, skyr, and fresh rye bread
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Icelandair Saga Lounge at Keflavík Airport — enjoy Icelandic snacks, local cheeses, and a farewell glass of Brennivín (Icelandic schnapps)
meals.dinner: In-flight dining on Icelandair (Saga Class if available) or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight time and work backward to schedule the airport transfer. Keflavík Airport is approximately 45–50 minutes from central Reykjavik in normal conditions but allow extra time in January for potential weather delays. Duty-free shopping at Keflavík is excellent for Icelandic spirits (Brennivín, Flóki Whisky), Nói Síríus chocolate, and premium Icelandic skincare products. Ensure all aurora photos are backed up before departure!
